title: Corpus report
description: The output of Corpus.Collect: every shard of the job's task list in task order with how it ended - the verdict of its accepted result with its product blobs and content hash, Disputed (its copies disagreed and no majority of three machines settled it) or NoResult with a fixed reason (no machine returned a result that could be accepted) - and the aggregate over the accepted results. The shards, their indexes and their URLs are the server's own task list; nothing a node returns can add, remove or rename one. Version 5: version 4 and two root objects, sampling (the share of the packages the run asked to run on two machines and what came back of it, in a word and in a sentence) and rounds (for each round the task packages that went out and the answers that came back): a run whose checking did not happen says so, and its numbers need not be held against the options it was started with. The integrity document carries the same two. Version 4: version 3 said, for every shard, how many shards the machine that ran it processes at once (degree): a fact about a machine, not about a shard, and gone. Version 3: version 2 took the index and the URL from the node's result and chose between the executions of a sampled shard by their content hashes.

controller.description: The controller version that wrote the report.

tasks.description: The shards of the job: the task list Corpus.Split made, whatever came back.

verdicts.description: Shards per verdict, Disputed and NoResult among them.

single_execution.description: Shards whose accepted result is one machine's word: not sampled, or the copy came back as a node fault or did not come back. Nothing compared it.

rejected_results.description: Values the server dropped: under no ticket of this job and round, no result or shaped as no honest node shapes one, claiming another controller version, not what their task asked for, or more under one ticket than a round takes. The integrity document counts them by reason.

repairs.description: Shards sent out once more because the first round left them without a result (a node fault, a dropped value, no answer): on two machines when the run asked for sampling, on one otherwise.

disputes.description: Shards whose copies disagreed, in the first round or in the repair round: each was run again on up to three machines.

disputes_resolved.description: Of those, the ones settled: one result was returned by the most machines, two at least, without a tie. The others are Disputed.

drops.description: Documents dropped per rule, summed over the completed shards.

languages.description: Documents out per ISO 639-3 code, summed over the completed shards.

unsupported_languages.description: Documents dropped as language_unsupported, by where they were nearest: the code of a language the pack knows and does not support, past_limit:<code> for a supported language the document lies past the limit of (a language the pack has no profile for, or text too unlike its own), no_profile for text that shares no n-gram with any profile. Sums to the drop language_unsupported; absent from reports of controllers before 0.2.0. Summed over the completed shards.

pdf_in.description: PDF responses the PDF stage took (WARC; present only where a shard met a PDF, like every pdf_* count).

pdf_truncated.description: Of those, the ones the crawler cut short (WARC-Truncated); read all the same.

pdf_extracted.description: PDFs that gave at least one page-range document.

pdf_documents.description: The page-range documents made (url#page=a-b); each also counts in documents_extracted.

pdf_pages_cut.description: Pages longer than a document may be (5,000 words), cut after the last line that fits.

pdf_running_lines.description: Lines removed as running headers and footers.

pdf_fuel.description: Fuel the PDF sandbox burned, counted from each run's _start: the same on every node.

funnel.description: The run's funnel over the completed shards: the records read, the documents extracted, the documents left after the language stage, the line stage and the quality filter, and the documents out (equal to quality); dropped sums the drops by the stage that applies them (extract counts records and PDFs that gave no document, beside the funnel; the others count documents). Absent from reports of controllers before 0.3.0.

output.description: What the run kept on the server: full, or stats_and_hashes (no text, no signatures: text_blob and signatures_blob are "", and Corpus.Dedup refuses the run). Absent from reports of controllers before 0.3.0 (they kept everything).

minhash.description: The MinHash parameters every shard's signatures were made with (kept or not); absent when no shard made signatures or the shards differ (each shard then says its own), and from reports of controllers before 0.3.0 (the defaults).

url.description: The shard's URL, from the server's task.

verdict.description: How the shard ended. The first seven are verdicts on the shard, the same on any honest node. Disputed: its copies disagreed and three machines did not settle it; it has no product and is out of the counts. NoResult: no machine returned a result that could be accepted, after one more try; reason says why. A node's own trouble is never a verdict.

reason.description: Present on NoResult: node_fault (a machine that held the shard returned it as a fault of its own; faults names the codes), no_answer (nothing that was accepted came back for it: nothing at all, or only values that were dropped).

executions.description: How many results the accepted one rests on: 1 is one machine's word, 2 a pair that agreed (in the first round, or in the repair round of a run that samples), 2 or 3 the majority of a dispute; 0 for Disputed and NoResult.

faults.description: Present when a node returned the shard as a fault of its own in any round: the fault codes, each once. A shard with a fault and a result was made by another machine or on the second try.

text_blob.description: Blob id of the zstd JSON lines, or "".

signatures_blob.description: Blob id of the signatures, or "".

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the uncompressed JSON lines: the identity a re-execution must reproduce.

error.description: A fixed code, never free text: why the shard did not complete (http_ and the three digits of the origin's status, hash_mismatch, body_truncated, oversized, oversized_unpacked, oversized_declared, not_warc, bad_compression, origin_not_allowed, origin_not_listed, origin_address, origin_redirect, no_language_model, language_model_refused, task_invalid), truncated on a completed shard whose file ends inside a record, or empty.

runtime_target.description: The operating system and architecture the shard ran on, e.g. "linux-x64" ("" from a controller before it was reported). A platform, never a machine.

minhash.description: The MinHash parameters the shard's signatures were made with; present when signatures were made, kept or not (absent from reports of controllers before 0.3.0, whose signatures carry the defaults).

signatures_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the shard's signatures blob as the node made it, kept or not (under stats_and_hashes it is made and hashed, not uploaded); empty when no signature was made. Absent from reports of controllers before 0.3.0.

bytes_produced.description: Bytes of the compressed text product; under output stats_and_hashes the size the product had on the node before it was deleted.

wait_ms.description: Time the shard waited on the node for a download slot and a processing slot.

drops.description: Documents dropped per rule; the PDF stage's are pdf_encrypted, pdf_unreadable, pdf_no_pages, pdf_fuel, pdf_memory, pdf_trap, pdf_error, pdf_oversized and pdf_empty.

unsupported_languages.description: Documents dropped as language_unsupported, by where they were nearest: the code of a language the pack knows and does not support, past_limit:<code> for a supported language the document lies past the limit of (a language the pack has no profile for, or text too unlike its own), no_profile for text that shares no n-gram with any profile. Sums to the drop language_unsupported; absent from reports of controllers before 0.2.0.

pdf_in.description: PDF responses the PDF stage took (WARC; present only where a shard met a PDF, like every pdf_* count).

pdf_truncated.description: Of those, the ones the crawler cut short (WARC-Truncated); read all the same.

pdf_extracted.description: PDFs that gave at least one page-range document.

pdf_documents.description: The page-range documents made (url#page=a-b); each also counts in documents_extracted.

pdf_pages_cut.description: Pages longer than a document may be (5,000 words), cut after the last line that fits.

pdf_running_lines.description: Lines removed as running headers and footers.

pdf_fuel.description: Fuel the PDF sandbox burned, counted from each run's _start: the same on every node.

sampling.description: What the run asked for in second executions and what came back of it in the first round. The platform picks the packages that run twice and does not say which, so the server counts: how many packages the rate comes to, how many came back with a second answer, how many shards had two results that were compared.

rate.description: The share of the packages the run asked to run on two machines (CorpusOptions.SamplingRate held to 0..1); null when the script did not hand the run's options to the activity that wrote the document.

state.description: The account in a word. not_asked: the run asked for no second execution. as_asked: as many packages came back twice as were asked for, and shards were compared. short: fewer packages came back twice than were asked for, so some of the checking did not happen. none: second executions were asked for and no shard was compared, so the checking did not happen (a pool of one machine ends here). unknown: rate is null.

packages.description: The task packages of the first round (a package is one shard in a job of up to 1,024 shards).

asked_twice.description: The packages the rate comes to by the platform's rule: rounded up, one at least when the rate is above 0; 0 when the rate is 0 or null.

answered_twice.description: The packages two answers or more came back for.

compared.description: The shards whose first two values of the first round were both results, and were compared.

statement.description: The same account in a sentence of fixed words, with the numbers in it.

rounds.description: How each round's fan-out came back, counted before any answer is opened: an answer counts whatever it held (results, a fault of its node, nothing readable). A round that was not run has zeros.

first.description: The first round: every package once, and the ones the platform picked for the run's sampling a second time on another machine.

repair.description: The repair round: the shards the first round left without a result, on two machines when the run asked for sampling, on one otherwise.

dispute.description: The dispute round: the shards whose copies disagreed, on three machines.

packages.description: The task packages that went out.

answers.description: The answers that came back under the round's tickets.

unanswered.description: The packages no answer came back for.

answered_once.description: The packages one answer came back for.

answered_twice.description: The packages two answers came back for.

answered_thrice.description: The packages three answers came back for.

answered_more.description: The packages more than three answers came back for.

counts.description: Name to count, names in ordinal order.
